stories.headline: Trumbull Congregational Church hosts Blessing of the Animals on Oct. 4
stories.summary: Trumbull Congregational Church will again welcome pets for a Blessing of the Animals on Sunday, Oct. 4, at 3 p.m. outdoors at 3115 Reservoir Avenue. Pastor Todd Shipley will lead the ceremony with his dachshund, Henry Houndsworth Longfellow. Owners can receive a paw-print certificate with a modest donation, browse pet toys and treats from Fairfield nonprofit Team Woofgang & Co., and enjoy refreshments, a bake sale, and live music. The event is open to all local residents; contact the church at office@trumbullcc.org or (203) 268-2433 for details.

stories.headline: Fairfield hosts e-bike safety panel tonight at Ludlowe High School
stories.summary: The Fairfield Safe Streets Alliance is holding a free community panel on e-bike rules, crash prevention, and shared-road safety Thursday, Oct. 1, from 7 to 8:30 p.m. at Fairfield Ludlowe High School. First Selectperson Christine Vitale said teens are riding more but may not know road rules, and residents worry about rider and driver safety. Speakers include police Sgt. Michael Komm, ER physician Dr. Douglas Latham, and crash survivors John Bysiewicz and Jenny Glass, followed by public Q&A and info tables from police, fire, hospitals, and bike groups. No taxpayer dollars fund the MetroCOG-supported campaign.

stories.headline: Supreme Court will hear Trump’s mandatory ICE detention-without-bond policy
stories.summary: The Supreme Court said Thursday it will decide whether the Trump administration can hold tens of thousands of immigrants in removal proceedings without bond hearings. The case, Rhoney v. Barbosa da Cunha, challenges ICE’s mandatory detention policy for people in the U.S. illegally, including longtime residents without criminal records. Appeals courts are split—two allow detention without bond, nine require bond eligibility for some detainees. The lead plaintiff, a Brazilian asylum applicant with a work permit, was released after a New York judge ordered a hearing; the Second Circuit called the policy the broadest mass-detention-without-bond mandate in U.S. history. Arguments come in the new term starting Monday.

stories.headline: Penguins’ 7–0 Flyers rout sets franchise records and Silovs milestone
stories.summary: Pittsburgh’s 7–0 season-opening win in Philadelphia was more than a blowout: historian Bob Grove noted it was the Penguins’ largest margin over the Flyers in Philly and their most decisive opener since 1995. Arturs Silovs became the first Penguins goalie with consecutive season-opening shutouts after blanking the Rangers last year. Sidney Crosby’s assist pushed him to an NHL-record 140 regular-season points against Philly; Evgeni Malkin’s power-play goal was his 100th point versus the Flyers. Debutant Nick Robertson scored twice, including his first career shorthanded goal. Home opener: Canadiens on Saturday at PPG Paints Arena.

stories.headline: Jets sign OL Kohl Levao to the active roster ahead of Bears week
stories.summary: Before Thursday’s practice, the Jets signed offensive lineman Kohl Levao (6-6, 350) from the practice squad to the 53-man roster. The Hawaii product played all three preseason games and spent most of last season on the practice squad after time with the USFL’s San Antonio Brahmas. New York also returned CB Jordan Clark and K Blake Grupe to the practice squad and released S John Saunders Jr. Grupe previously hit all 11 field goals for Indianapolis late in 2025, including a 60-yarder. The moves come as the Jets prepare for Chicago amid a heavy Week 4 injury list.

stories.headline: Apple Stores get ‘Do Not Open Until October 8’ boxes ahead of smart-home launch
stories.summary: Apple retail stores worldwide received confidential merchandise boxes stamped “Do Not Open Until October 8,” MacRumors verified Thursday. The materials are expected to prep displays for a rumored Oct. 13 smart-home push: a new hub device, an updated HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K, following Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. The boxes could relate to iPhone Duo marketing, but timing and secrecy point more toward the hub trio that would need floor updates if announced the week of Oct. 5. Exact announcement versus on-sale timing for Oct. 13 remains unclear.

stories.headline: SpaceX Crew-13 lifts off for the ISS aboard Dragon Grace
stories.summary: Despite thunderstorm and wind concerns, SpaceX launched NASA’s Crew-13 mission Thursday from Cape Canaveral. Falcon 9 lofted Dragon capsule Grace with NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA’s Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov for up to six months on the International Space Station. Docking is expected about eight hours after liftoff. Watkins is on her second flight; Delaney, Kutryk, and Teteryatnikov are first-timers. The mission slipped from mid-September after an oxidizer leak during processing. Crew-13 will relieve Crew-12, due to splash down off Southern California next week.

stories.headline: Tesla 2026.38 sharpens HW3 visuals and adds dynamic headlight leveling
stories.summary: Tesla began rolling out software 2026.38 to Hardware 3 cars, with sharper on-screen vehicle visualizations for AMD Ryzen-equipped HW3 models and Dynamic Headlight Leveling for matrix-LED low beams that aim using vision AI. The headlight feature overlaps NHTSA recall 26V507 covering about 19,900 Model 3 and Y vehicles for low-beam glare; older cars without matrix LEDs still need a physical fix, and owner letters started Sept. 15. Early fleet data showed under 1% on the build. The update also includes security fixes; Intel Atom HW3 cars miss the sharper graphics.

stories.headline: Canon patents wild RF zooms—including a constant f/6.3 180–600mm
stories.summary: Canon Rumors highlighted patent filings for ambitious full-frame RF zooms: a 70–135mm f/2L IS, a 200–400mm f/4L IS, and a standout 180–600mm f/6.3L IS. Designs emphasize internal zoom with a stationary front group so less heavy glass moves, potentially faster zoom action and better sealing. The 180–600 would give Canon zoom reach where Sony and Nikon offer 600mm f/6.3 primes. Patents are not product announcements—Canon could alter or shelve them—but they sit alongside other recent fast-zoom concepts, including a previously reported 20–60mm f/2L.

stories.headline: 2027 Jeep Cherokee Trailhawk earns Trail Rated status with locker and low range
stories.summary: Jeep unveiled the 2027 Cherokee Trailhawk this week, finally giving the hybrid Cherokee Trail Rated hardware: a locking rear axle, two-speed transfer case (2.92:1 low / 37.5:1 crawl), nine inches of ground clearance, 245/65R17 all-terrains, and steel skid plates including hybrid-battery protection. Approach, departure, and breakover angles are claimed best-in-class, with 24-inch wading depth. Power stays 210 hp / 230 lb-ft turbo-hybrid with E-CVT and EPA estimates of 33/29/31 mpg. Pricing starts at $44,625 including destination; order books are open, production later this year.

stories.headline: Texas Renaissance Festival’s 52nd season opens Oct. 10 under new ownership
stories.summary: The Texas Renaissance Festival in Todd Mission opens Oct. 10 for weekends through Nov. 29 plus Black Friday—its first full season after founder George Coulam’s 2025 death and a court-ordered $60 million sale to investor Meril Rivard. Operators say the on-ground experience stays familiar under the “Magic and Memories” theme: 21 stages, nearly 500 shops, jousting, and themed weekends from Oktoberfest to Celtic Christmas. The Fields of New Market campgrounds span 230+ acres; SH 249’s Grimes County extension eases access. Tickets are date-specific; prop weapons must be sheathed and peace-tied.

stories.headline: LEGO UCS Executor review: 6,130 pieces, 53.5 inches—longer than a dining table
stories.summary: GamesRadar’s hands-on review of LEGO Star Wars 75457 Executor Super Star Destroyer calls the $799.99 / 6,130-piece UCS set the longest LEGO Star Wars model ever at 53.5 inches (136 cm). The ~15-hour build improves on 2011’s 10221 with ILM-accurate proportions, unique printed “light opening” tiles, zero stickers, and all six Empire Strikes Back bounty hunters plus Vader—though Admiral Piett is missing. Verdict: a gold-standard UCS if you can afford the price and shelf space; weak spots include no interior and some delicate panelling.

stories.headline: Shenandoah fall travel: weekday tips, Skyline Drive entrances, and color updates
stories.summary: Shenandoah National Park’s fall season runs late September through November, with cool days (roughly 49–60°F) and heavy weekend crowds. NPS urges buying entrance passes ahead, arriving midweek, and using southern entrances (Swift Run or Rockfish) when Front Royal and Thornton Gap back up. Campgrounds and lodges book out months ahead; first-come sites often fill by Thursday evening. Old Rag parking is limited on October Saturdays. Weekly Thursday fall-update videos plus valley and Big Meadows webcams help track color across the park’s 100-mile, multi-elevation stretch—peak timing can’t be pinned to one day.

stories.headline: Gurman: touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro could arrive as early as October
stories.summary: On Bloomberg’s Power On podcast Thursday, Mark Gurman said he believes Apple will introduce its first touchscreen MacBook Pro models this fall—“as early as October,” possibly slipping to November. The 14- and 16-inch machines are rumored with OLED touch displays, M5 Pro/Max chips, a thinner chassis, and a Dynamic Island instead of a notch, tested on macOS 27.2 (expected late October). They would sit above regular MacBook Pros slated for M7 next year; branding could stay MacBook Pro or shift to something like MacBook Ultra. Cellular Mac hopes remain speculative.
